title: Shadowline shift manifest
content:
Shift: Shadowline (02:00–10:00 PT)
Owner: Priya Shah (on call) — notes for the next person

Purpose: lightweight, stick-to-the-essentials passdown for common incidents and ongoing experiments. This is a personal scratch/runbook draft — contains trial commands, mental notes, and TODOs. Not final policy.

CURRENT STATE (what I left for next):
- No active P0s. Last cleared: elevated-redis-queue-io (INF-5987) — mitigated via scaled read replicas at 00:45 PST, CPU back to normal.
- Two alerts firing but low severity: 1) slow-embed-warmup (latency spikes when embedding model instances scale up) — noisy on peeks, not affecting 99% success; 2) kv-cache-miss-rate above baseline for customer "mosaic" (see metrics below).
- Running nightly rollout: quantized-gptq v2 -> traffic fraction 10% on cluster-a; watch for parity regressions (SLOs tracked under /product/hosted-api/rollouts).

KEY METRICS SNAPSHOT (from 01:30 UTC):
- Platform-wide p95 latency: 152ms (target <160ms)
- Token throughput (last 5m): 420k tokens/min
- 5xx rate: 0.09% (target <0.25%)
- KV cache miss rate (global): 18% (typical 6–12%) — spike concentrated on tag prefix "mosaic/2026-03"

QUICK TROUBLESHOOT CHECKLIST (first 10 minutes)
1) If p95 > 250ms: check recent deploys (git sha -> /deployments), then check autoscaler logs for GPU contention: kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/auto-scaler --since=10m
2) If 5xx > 0.5%: tail api-gateway logs and look for specific error classes (OOM, rate-limit, upstream 502). Example: gcloud logging read 'resource.type="k8s_container" AND labels.k8s-pod/app="api-gateway"' --limit 200 --project=redwood-prod
3) If KV cache miss storm: identify customers with high miss rate: ./tools/kv-metrics query --prefix mosaic/2026-03 --window 10m 
   - If miss rate persists > 25%, try cold-cache prefill for top 5 keys using prefiller script: tools/prefill_kv.sh --customer mosaic --top 5
4) If model node OOMs: check node-scratchpad available mem and restart offending pod with graceful restart: kubectl rollout restart statefulset/serve-model-<model-id>

RUNBOOK STEPS — common incidents
A) High KV cache miss (this was noisy tonight)
   - Symptoms: sudden spike in miss rate, correlated with increased embedding requests and scales.
   - Quick mitigation: temporarily increase cache size for the shard or bump TTL for hot prefix. Command: curl -XPOST $CACHE_ADMIN/api/v1/shards/shard-7/resize -d '{"target_mb":2048}' (ops token required).
   - If admin API unavailable: deploy temporary in-memory LRU layer (scripts/memory-layer-proxy) to shard hot keys and notify infra.
   - Long term: open follow-up INF ticket to investigate prefix skews and autoscaler heuristics (I added notes to INF-5987).

B) Latency regression after rollout (quantized model)
   - Symptoms: p95 increases, generation quality mismatch, higher RT tokens/time.
   - First step: rollback traffic to previous model variant in the console (hosted-api -> rollouts -> rollback). If console down, use API: curl -XPOST $API/rollouts/rollback -d '{"rollout_id":"r-842"}'
   - Capture sample prompts that regressed (console traces -> query by recent trace ids) and place in /product/hosted-api/rollouts/regression-samples/<timestamp>.

ESCALATION & CONTACTS
- Primary: Oncall SRE (me) — Priya Shah (Slack: @priya.s)
- Secondary: Maya Lopez (eng infra) — @maya.l (pager on call)
- Model infra lead: Ethan Zhou — @ethan.z (for model-serving-specific issues)
- Pager escalation path: S1 -> SRE oncall -> infra lead -> engineering manager oncall. Phone numbers and pager IDs are in internal/contacts (I keep the up-to-date list there).

OPEN ACTIONS / TODOs (for next shift)
- [ ] Follow up with infra on autoscaler config: heuristics for cold-start embedding instances. Assigned INF-6021 (Maya) — check status before 06:00 PT.
- [ ] Add prefill job to nightly pipeline for top mixer prefixes (I sketched prefill logic in tools/prefill_kv.sh but not deployed).
- [ ] Collect 10 regression prompts if quantized rollout shows quality drop — save to /product/hosted-api/rollouts/regression-samples/.
- [ ] Check the mem-leak hypothesis on serve-runtime v3.7.3 — I left sanitized heap dumps at s3://redwood-debug/heapdumps/2026-03-05/

NOTES TO SELF / HINTS
- If you see consistent "KV replica lag" messages in the logs, that's usually because the write path is being overwhelmed by backend ingestion (look at /backfill-job-*/metrics). Temporary fix: throttle backfill job: kubectl scale job/backfill-ingest --replicas=1
- For quick connection checks to GPU nodes: ssh gpu-node-<id> && nvidia-smi -q | grep "Compute Mode"
- Prefiller script uses ephemeral credentials; you'll need vault access (read-only token is fine) — I left a token note in 1Password (look for "shadowline-prefill").

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS (things I wanted to ask but ran out of time)
- Is the embedding warmup latency tied to model cache invalidations or the autoscaler cooldown windows? I suspect cooldown is too long for bursty traffic.
- Should we increase the default cache TTL for new customer prefixes by 2x? Will discuss with infra on Monday if not resolved.

HANDOFF CHECKLIST FOR NEXT PERSON (two-minute pass)
1) Confirm no P0s in PagerDuty and check Slack #incident-status.
2) Verify quantized rollout health: hosted-api/rollouts -> check p95 and error rate for variant v2.
3) Re-run the KV miss query: ./tools/kv-metrics query --prefix mosaic/2026-03 --window 15m and act if >25%.
4) Review open INF tickets assigned to "shadowline" and update notes.

END NOTES
- If you poke around and find fresh regressions, tag me @priya.s and leave a short blurb here with the time and metric snapshot.
- This doc is a scratchpad — if you rework any commands or make a small useful script, please push to tools/ and leave a short note.

Recent references: JIRA INF-5987 (kv miss), PR #842 (serve-runtime quantize tweak), Confluence page infra/kv-cache-behavior (design notes).

-- Priya
